Maya: Running into a puzzler while converting the SDK example to an edge SSR route (vite + tsup). TS loses inference on a generic overload and the worker throws 'foo is not a function' at runtime.
Theo: can you paste the snippet and tsconfig? often moduleResolution + preserveValueImports cause weirdness.
Maya: snippet:
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const c = createClient()
const out = await c.tool<{ rows: number }>('parse')
console.log(out.rows)
```
tsconfig: { "target":"es2022","module":"esnext","moduleResolution":"bundler","strict":true }
Rina: Vite/tsup sometimes resolve package exports differently than TS expects. If your bundler resolves to the CJS entry the emitted runtime shape differs (missing named exports) and types can collapse to unknown.
Theo: quick try: switch import to `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference/esm'` — if that fixes runtime, it points at an export map resolution problem (not a TS language bug).
Maya: named direct esm import fixed runtime but I don't want to ship samples pointing at internal paths.
Rina: long-term fix: add an explicit "types" condition in package.json exports for an edge-friendly d.ts (types/edge/index.d.ts) and add a tiny tsconfig.edge.json to examples so users get the right moduleResolution.
Theo: on types shape: our overloads use conditional mapped types to model tool outputs. When that cascades through conditional exports TS sometimes widens to unknown at the callsite. Short-term workaround: use a single generic method `tool<T = any>(...)` and provide a `decodeTool<T>(res)` helper for strict mode.
Maya: I prefer `unknown` over `any` for safety, but that adds boilerplate for quickstarts.
Rina: proposal: default package stays ergonomic (some `any` in top-level overloads) and we publish a `@redwood/inference/strict` types-only entry with fully strict signatures. Docs will show how to opt in.
Theo: another runtime issue: edge fetch errors look different (no `code`, no `syscall`) so our retry layer calls into node-specific cleanup (like `req.destroy()`) and blows up. We should normalize the error at the network boundary and avoid calling Node-only APIs.
Maya: small reproducible test: try building examples with rollup/esbuild/tsup + TS 4.9/5.x in CI to catch these resolver/type parity issues early. build-bot: pipeline failed for examples/edge-ssr (types) — https://ci.internal/edge/2042
Rina: action items:
- Theo: add `types/edge/index.d.ts` and update exports map so bundlers & TS pick a stable edge types entry (owner: Theo)
- Rina: add examples/edge/tsconfig.edge.json + README that recommends named imports and moduleResolution settings (owner: Rina)
- Maya: add a minimal repro under examples/edge-ssr and link the failing CI job (owner: Maya)
- All: decide on strict vs ergonomic typedefs (owner: team; proposal from Rina due EOD)
Theo: I'll also prototype an overload pattern that exposes a strict helper type instead of making top-level signatures strict by default.
Maya: thanks. I'll post the repro link when pushed. Ping #devex if you run into this — small repros speed fixes. :seedling:
